note: AMERICAN HEALTH INDEX — EXPLORATORY COMPOSITE. This is an analytical visualization, NOT an objective measurement of national worth (root Section 13). Method: 8 dimensions; each scored 0-100 per decade by min-max normalization of underlying indicators over their 1970-2024 range; equal weighting unless stated. Underlying indicators listed per dimension and disclosed in the explorer with adjustable weights. Scores are heuristic analyst judgments grounded in the indicator datasets — treat as directional, not precise.

human_wellbeing.weights: health 2x, social 2x, opportunity 1.5x, wealth 1.5x, freedom 1x, others 1x
human_wellbeing.note: Best view for ordinary living standards; 2020s less catastrophic here (income records, low unemployment, falling crime) but dragged by housing + health plateau

fiscal_sustainability.note: 2020s worst — debt, deficits, interest burden all at post-WWII extremes ex-crises

reading_guide: All models agree: 1990s and 1970s score best (for opposite reasons — 1970s: low inequality, fiscal calm, rising health despite stagflation; 1990s: growth, fiscal surpluses, falling crime). All models agree: 2020s score worst, driven by fiscal deterioration, wealth concentration, and the freedom/institutional collapse. The 2010s are middling: good social stability, bad inequality and institutions. The composite is NOT a verdict on national worth — it is a lens; change the weights and the ranking of decades changes materially.
